question: Does encoding-agnostic iterative decompression (sniff delivered bytes, try brotli→gzip→identity until SHA256 matches ground truth) restore byte-identical correctness through Cloudflare CDN for all 48 payload×order×chunk×Accept-Encoding conditions, and does it generalize to depths 3-5 and payloads >100KB?
hypothesis: An encoding-agnostic decoder that does not assume the origin's layer stack — instead sniffing the delivered bytes and iteratively attempting brotli, gzip, then identity decompression until SHA256 matches the ground truth — restores byte-identical correctness through Cloudflare CDN for all 48 tested conditions. This works because: (1) CDN re-encoding is lossless (parent forensic: iterative decode == ground truth on 24/24 JSON/HTML); (2) the failure is in the fixed-origin-order framing assumption, not byte corruption; (3) encoding-agnostic decode is agnostic to which transforms CDN applies.
falsifier: Any of the following falsifies the hypothesis: (1) any of the 48 CDN cells produces decompressed output with SHA256 != ground truth under encoding-agnostic decode; (2) encoding-agnostic decode fails for BINARY payload type (parent forensic only tested JSON/HTML); (3) CDN re-encoding at depth >2 or payload >100KB produces non-recoverable byte transformations; (4) identity payloads are corrupted (not just compressed) by CDN; (5) cache HIT staleness (if observed) causes different decompressed output than consecutive-serve.

baselines.description: Parent fixed-origin-order decompression on the same 48-cell matrix — re-validates the 60/240 (0.25) CDN correctness from EXP-RUNTIME-35538865067. If encoding-agnostic decode improves on this, it demonstrates the fix is real.
baselines.expected: 60/240 correct (parent result), with all failures in the same cells (non-GZIP-OUTER or non-gzip AE)

baselines.description: Same payloads served directly from localhost without CDN — re-validates parent 240/240 result and serves as ground-truth sanity check for the encoding-agnostic decoder itself.
baselines.expected: 240/240 byte-identical decompression output to ground truth (encoding-agnostic and fixed-order both pass)

baselines.description: Uncompressed (identity) payloads served through CDN — tests whether CDN corrupts or merely compresses uncompressed data. Parent found 5/15 byte-identical (BINARY 5/5 passthrough, JSON/HTML gzip-compressed by CDN).
baselines.expected: Encoding-agnostic decode recovers ground truth for all 15 identity observations (CDN may gzip-compress text types, which encoding-agnostic decode handles)

baselines.description: Encoding-agnostic decode applied to depths 3-5 (triple and quadruple stacked encodings: brotli(q4)+gzip(L1)+brotli(q4), etc.) served through CDN. Tests whether the fix generalizes beyond depth-2.
baselines.expected: Encoding-agnostic decode recovers ground truth for all depth>2 CDN observations

baselines.description: Encoding-agnostic decode applied to >100KB payloads served through CDN. Tests whether large-payload CDN behavior (TCP segmentation, chunked transfer) breaks the fix.
baselines.expected: Encoding-agnostic decode recovers ground truth for all >100KB CDN observations

positive_control: B-LOCALHOST-DIRECT: encoding-agnostic decode on localhost-served payloads matches ground truth — re-validates parent 240/240. If this fails, the decoder implementation is broken and no CDN inference is possible.
null_control: B-CDN-IDENTITY: encoding-agnostic decode on uncompressed CDN payloads recovers ground truth. If CDN corrupts uncompressed data, compressed data cannot be trusted. Additionally, encoding-agnostic decode on localhost identity must be trivially 15/15 (identity passthrough).
measurement_validity: Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared) must be installed and functional — verify /health endpoint returns HTTP 200 through public URL before measuring
Each CDN-served request must record the actual delivered Content-Encoding header and raw wire bytes

Encoding-agnostic decode algorithm: try brotli.decompress(raw_bytes), if valid compare SHA256 to ground truth; else try gzip.decompress(raw_bytes), if valid compare; else compare raw_bytes SHA256 to ground truth (identity)
Minimum N=5 observations per condition with jitter 200-500ms between CDN requests to avoid cache collapse
Unique URLs per main-matrix observation plus Cache-Control: public, max-age=0 or no-cache to test fresh serving
Ground truth computed as SHA256 of full-body iterative decode (same as parent): for each origin-compressed payload, decompress all layers to produce the reference SHA256
Depths 3-5: generate payloads with 3-5 stacked compression layers (alternating brotli q4 and gzip L1), serve through CDN, apply encoding-agnostic decode
Large payloads: generate >100KB high-entropy payloads, compress with 2-layer stacking, serve through CDN, apply encoding-agnostic decode
BINARY payloads: within-run ground truth only (PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent; cross-run comparison not valid)
Environment: Python 3.12+, brotli 1.2.0, requests 2.x or http.client, cloudflared tunnel
decision_rule:
ALL conditions must pass for SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST:
- C1: Encoding-agnostic decode produces byte-identical SHA256 output as ground truth for ALL 48 primary CDN cells (3 payload × 2 orders × 2 chunk sizes × 4 Accept-Encoding variants)
- C2: Encoding-agnostic decode recovers ground truth for BINARY CDN cells (parent forensic did not fully test BINARY)
- C3: CDN consecutive-serve stability preserved: 3 identical requests to same URL produce identical decompressed output under encoding-agnostic decode
- C4: Identity payloads pass through CDN with encoding-agnostic decode recovering ground truth (B-CDN-IDENTITY)
- C5: Depth generalization: encoding-agnostic decode recovers ground truth for at least 80% of depth 3-5 CDN observations
- C6: Large payload: encoding-agnostic decode recovers ground truth for at least 80% of >100KB CDN observations
- Positive control passes: B-LOCALHOST-DIRECT encoding-agnostic decode matches ground truth (240/240)
- Null control passes: B-CDN-IDENTITY encoding-agnostic decode recovers ground truth
IF C1 fails: FALSIFIES — encoding-agnostic decode does not restore correctness; diagnose which cells fail
IF C1 passes but C5/C6 fail: MIXED — primary gate passes but generalization is bounded
IF all pass: SUPPORTS — C-MEAS-VALID ready for Product Core promotion (only kernel integration remains)
product_consequence_positive: CDN decompression gate closes. Encoding-agnostic decode validated through real CDN for all tested conditions. C-MEAS-VALID is ready for Product Core promotion — only kernel integration of the encoding-agnostic decoder remains. This unblocks the full decompression chain validation across localhost AND real CDN.
product_consequence_negative: Encoding-agnostic decode fails on some CDN conditions — C-MEAS-VALID remains blocked from Product Core. Diagnosis of which cells fail identifies whether the issue is: (a) specific encoding combinations not handled by try-brotli→gzip→identity order, (b) CDN corruption at depth >2, (c) large-payload TCP segmentation effects, or (d) BINARY-specific ground-truth reproducibility.
estimated_cost: Low: same infrastructure as parent (cloudflared, Python HTTP server, brotli library). Additional payload generation for depths 3-5 and >100KB adds ~5 minutes. Estimated total wall time 15-20 minutes.
expected_information_gain: Very high: this is the sole remaining blocker for C-MEAS-VALID Product Core promotion per parent handoff. A positive result closes the CDN gate and enables promotion. A negative result identifies the specific remaining fix needed. Both outcomes directly change a product decision. The experiment is the smallest possible test that can resolve the inherited unknown.
